subtopics.title: Economic Systems and the Four Factors

questions.question: Economic systems are distinguished by:
options: Who answers the three questions — what, how and for whom to produce

questions.question: The practical weakness of central planning is that:
options: Without price signals, gluts pile up beside shortages and effort goes unrewarded
Too many firms enter each market

questions.question: South Africa's economy carries the extra label DUALISTIC because:
options: A first-world financial economy runs alongside a vast informal and subsistence economy

questions.question: Profit is called the RESIDUAL because it:
options: Is fixed by law each year
Is paid before wages and rent
Is whatever remains after rent, wages and interest are settled — and can be negative

subtopics.title: Measuring and Mapping the Economy — Aggregates, Sectors and Infrastructure

questions.question: The three GDP methods that must reconcile are:
options: Production (value added), income (factor rewards) and expenditure (final spending)

questions.question: In the expenditure method, G includes:
options: The salaries of nurses, teachers and police — government consumption, not grants

questions.question: South Africa's long structural arc shows:
options: Mining now producing most of GDP
Manufacturing doubling its share every decade
A shrinking primary share, sideways manufacturing, and services near two-thirds of GDP

questions.question: The load-shedding years demonstrate that infrastructure is:
options: The skeleton every sector hangs on — when it fails, production, small firms and investment all suffer

subtopics.title: Markets at Work — Elasticity, Costs and Revenue

questions.question: Price elasticity of demand is calculated as:
options: Percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price
Total revenue divided by total cost
Change in price divided by change in income

questions.question: The strongest determinant pushing demand toward ELASTIC is:
options: The good taking a tiny share of income
Having no time to shop around

questions.question: Facing inelastic demand, a price rise:
options: Raises total revenue — the few customers lost are outweighed by the higher price on those who stay

questions.question: A price-taking firm maximises profit by producing where:

subtopics.title: Connected Markets and the Two Policies

questions.question: When butter's price jumps, the market for margarine experiences:
options: A rightward SHIFT of the demand curve, because the goods are substitutes
A leftward shift of the supply curve
A movement along an unchanged demand curve

questions.question: The demand for labour is DERIVED because:
options: Wages are set by the state
Workers are hired only because someone is buying the product their work builds

questions.question: The Reserve Bank's primary mandate and lever are:
options: Price stability with inflation targeted at three to six percent, using the repo rate

questions.question: A correct speed comparison of the two policies is:
options: Both adjust only once a decade
The budget changes daily while the repo waits a year
The repo rate adjusts in an afternoon while the budget turns annually

subtopics.title: Three Kitchens and Four Pay Packets

questions.question: In kitchen two, Tuesday drowns in soup while Thursday runs out of bread because:
options: The distant office cannot see the queue — planning lacks price signals

questions.question: The mixed economy is kitchen three because:
options: No one may cook without a permit
The queue decides the menu while the state inspects, taxes and feeds those who cannot pay

questions.question: The owner's envelope differs from the other three because profit:
options: Is fixed by the stand fee
Is the leftover after rent, wages and interest — the only envelope that can be empty

subtopics.title: Rubber Bands, Planks and the Next Plate

questions.question: Chips with a rival brand on the shelf behave as a rubber band because:
options: Substitutes let buyers bounce away when the price rises — elastic demand
Chips take most of the budget
There is no formula for snacks

questions.question: The taxi fare to school is a plank because:
options: Fares are set by the Reserve Bank
It is a necessity with no real substitute, so riders still ride — inelastic demand
The fare is a luxury item

questions.question: Raising the price of a rubber-band good typically:
options: Shrinks the till — customers scatter faster than the higher price compensates

questions.question: At a fifteen-rand market price, the vetkoek stall should stop frying when:
options: The stand fee has been covered
The next vetkoek costs more than fifteen rand to make — marginal cost passes marginal revenue

subtopics.title: The Till Slip and the Two Drivers

questions.question: Counting final goods only prevents:
options: Double counting — the flour being counted alone and again inside the vetkoek

questions.question: The three departments of the national till slip are:
options: Out of the earth, through the works, across the counter — primary, secondary, tertiary

questions.question: Driver one at the Reserve Bank steers by:
options: Choosing what to tax from payslips
Pressing the repo pedal — costlier or cheaper borrowing within weeks — to hold inflation at three to six percent

questions.question: When driver two spends beyond the tax take, the gap:
options: Is paid by the Reserve Bank's profits
Is borrowed, and the interest quietly eats a growing slice of future budgets
